Volume Skin Color: regression against DAZ Studio

Diffeomorphic DAZ Importer, Extended Principled material method, option off (today) vs on (Volume Skin Color).

Method. 236 Genesis 8 / 8.1 / 9 characters, each saved as a scene in DAZ Studio and exported with its .dbz, imported with Easy Import defaults. Rendered in Blender (Cycles, GPU, 4x samples + denoiser) and in DAZ Studio (Iray) with the same camera and the same light (grey world 0.4 plus one sun; DAZ calibrated to Blender with a chart). Number: colour difference ΔE (CIELAB 1976) of the average face colour against the DAZ render, plus its lightness part dL and chroma part dC (+ = more than DAZ). Below about 2 is hard to see.

Worse by more than 1: one PBR Skin figure (0.8 → 2.3, slightly light) and one fur figure whose DAZ look is fur Blender does not render. With the option off, every material node tree is identical to the current build (all 236 figures compared node by node).

A second light

12 of the figures again, under a different light in both programs: no sun, a warm sky above and a dim cool ground below. This light has no chart calibration, so one exposure factor (×0.615) was fitted on the four control figures of the unchanged import and applied to every Blender render. Controls are figures that already matched DAZ.

Known limits

  • Scope. One checkbox, Volume Skin Color (Global Settings > Materials), off by default. Only the Extended Principled material method changes; BSDF and FBX Compatible build exactly as before. Iray Uber surfaces that are thin walled, and surfaces with a constant base colour (no texture or colour-effect group), keep the current build.
  • Lightness. PBR Skin comes out slightly light: median +1.3 L* against DAZ Studio.
  • Shine. Specular, dual-lobe and top-coat are not touched. Figures whose difference is shine (for example Diana, +4.4 L*) stay off by that amount.
  • Flat Translucency Colors. A saturated Translucency Color without a texture reaches about 80 % of DAZ Studio's colour shift.
  • Eyes. Sclera, iris and pupils come out a little lighter than in DAZ Studio (about 2.5 dE on the eye pixels, not visible side by side). K assumes a deep layer, which describes the eye's thin shell less well.
  • Colour values. PBR Skin uses SSS Color and Transmitted Color as displayed; Iray Uber uses them linearised (displayed^2.2), which is what matched DAZ Studio for each. The difference between the two shaders is deliberate.
  • Import time. K is computed once per material at import (fixed-seed random walk, cached per input): about +2 s per figure, up to +5 s; surfaces that barely absorb (eyes) take longest.
  • Tested. Windows; Blender 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 5.2 and 5.3; Cycles and Eevee; 236 Genesis 8 / 8.1 / 9 figures against DAZ Studio renders under the same light, 12 of them also under a second light. Not tested: macOS / Linux, Genesis 3 and older.
